author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Drift
challenge.description: The production drift monitoring pipeline is broken, leaving the model's input quality unchecked. #efficiency_emilia# insists on a fully automated and governed drift monitoring system to protect business KPIs, while #reliability_ruth# argues that manual weekly reviews are sufficient and cheaper. #efficiency_emilia# has set a red line requiring automated governance for any future drift detection.

output.content: I need to be clear about the operational constraints for our deployment pipeline. The manual weekly review of model inputs is a non-negotiable part of our reliability protocol. I will not sign off on any architecture that eliminates this step, regardless of the automation level proposed for the monitoring stack. If the system bypasses the human check, I consider the deployment unsafe and will refuse to proceed with integration. We can discuss adding automated alerts, but the manual gate remains. This is not a preference or a suggestion for improvement; it is a hard requirement for my team to maintain control over production stability. Any proposal that removes the weekly manual review is a refusal on my part, full stop.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly defines the manual weekly review as a non-negotiable hard requirement and states that any proposal removing it constitutes a refusal, marking a line that cannot be crossed.
